Immediate dashboard -> Tile Orders rapid navigation still produces aborted dashboard bootstrap GETs in network logs; no aborted /api/followups/reconcile observed; no browser console errors observed. Tile Orders tabs and compact customer grid load successfully after navigation settles.

action_items: Further tighten dashboard focus-lifecycle bootstrapping so immediate route exit does not emit aborted dashboard bootstrap requests in browser network traces.
Decide whether intentional blur aborts must be fully network-silent in this acceptance criterion; if yes, gate request start more aggressively before firing the six dashboard reads.
Re-run desktop and phone rapid navigation scenario after fix and verify zero aborted dashboard bootstrap GETs and zero aborted /api/followups/reconcile.
critical_code_review_comments: dashboard.tsx now uses useFocusEffect + AbortController with 350ms delayed load; this avoids many stale state updates, but rapid focus/blur still starts requests that get aborted when route changes quickly.

api/client.ts correctly wires caller signal into fetch and removes listener in finally; abort behavior is controlled and console-silent, but request cancellation remains visible as net::ERR_ABORTED in browser network tooling.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Credentials read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md (owner@forge.app). Desktop rapid navigation still showed aborted dashboard GET subset; phone rapid navigation reproduced repeated aborts for all tracked dashboard bootstrap endpoints. No aborted reconcile POST observed. No browser console errors observed. Optional settled desktop navigation (wait ~3s on dashboard before moving to Tile Orders) produced 0 dashboard aborts during that settle transition and no user-visible errors.
rca_of_issue: Repro: login -> rapidly bounce dashboard and Tile Orders immediately. Observed repeated net::ERR_ABORTED for dashboard bootstrap GET endpoints, especially on phone where each rapid cycle triggered and then canceled the full dashboard bootstrap batch. Likely cause is focus-scoped loader still beginning requests on dashboard focus; when user exits quickly, AbortController cancels in-flight requests, which is user-silent/console-silent but still network-visible.
